/-!
# Conjecture 9.78

by V. P. Shunkov

Does there exist a periodic residually finite $F^{*}$-group (see Archive, 7.42) all of
whose Sylow subgroups are finite and which is not binary finite?

Here a group $G$ is an $F^{*}$-group in the sense of V. P. Shunkov (Kourovka Notebook,
Archive, 7.42) if for every finite subgroup $H$ of $G$ and every element $a$ of prime order
in $N_G(H)/H$, all the subgroups $\langle a, a^g \rangle$, $g \in N_G(H)/H$, are finite.
A Sylow $p$-subgroup of an arbitrary group is a maximal $p$-subgroup. A group is
*binary finite* if any two of its elements generate a finite subgroup.

The requirement that the group be residually finite is what distinguishes this problem
from Archive problem 7.42.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

def IsResiduallyFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N
blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is *residually finite* if every non-identity element lies outside some
normal subgroup of finite index, i.e. the intersection of all normal subgroups of finite
index of $G$ is trivial.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Subgroup.FiniteIndex / Subgroup.Normal (used as building blocks); no existing predicate on groups.
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.78».IsResiduallyFinite
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of residually finite group (grep for 'ResiduallyFinite'/'residually' in Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib finds nothing). Defined as: every g ≠ 1 lies outside some normal subgroup of finite index (`N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N`), i.e. the intersection of the finite-index normal subgroups is trivial — the standard definition.

/-- A group $G$ is *residually finite* if every non-identity element lies outside some
normal subgroup of finite index, i.e. the intersection of all normal subgroups of finite
index of $G$ is trivial. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

A group $G$ is an *$F^{*}$-group* (V. P. Shunkov, Kourovka Notebook, Archive, 7.42) if
for every finite subgroup $H$ of $G$ and every element $a$ of prime order in the quotient

justification.closest_existing_considered: Nothing comparable; Mathlib has `Subgroup.normalizer`, `Subgroup.subgroupOf`, `QuotientGroup`, `orderOf`, which are used as building blocks.
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.78».IsFStarGroup
justification.why_needed: Shunkov's F*-groups (Kourovka Archive 7.42) have no Mathlib counterpart. Defined as: for every finite subgroup H, and all a, g in N_G(H)/H (formalized as `H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer`, a group via Mathlib's `Subgroup.normal_in_normalizer`), if `orderOf a` is prime then `Subgroup.closure {a, g⁻¹ * a * g}` is finite. H ranges over all finite subgroups including the trivial one.

blocks.name: IsFStarGroup
blocks.text:
/-- A group $G$ is an *$F^{*}$-group* (V. P. Shunkov, Kourovka Notebook, Archive, 7.42) if
for every finite subgroup $H$ of $G$ and every element $a$ of prime order in the quotient
$N_G(H)/H$, the subgroups $\langle a, a^g \rangle$, $g \in N_G(H)/H$, are all finite.
Here $a^g = g^{-1} a g$. -/
def IsFStarGroup : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H →
    ∀ a g : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      (orderOf a).Prime → Finite (Subgroup.closure {a, g⁻¹ * a * g})

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBinaryFinite.isFStarGroup (hG : IsBinaryFinite G) : IsFStarGroup G := by
  intro H _ a g _
  induction a using QuotientGroup.induction_on with | H a
  induction g using QuotientGroup.induction_on with | H g
  -- `⟨a, a^g⟩` is finite in `N_G(H)`: it embeds into the finite subgroup `⟨a, a^g⟩` of `G`.
  have h₁ : (Subgroup.closure {a, g⁻¹ * a * g} : Set H.normalizer).Finite := by
    refine Set.Finite.of_finite_image (f := H.normalizer.subtype) ?_
      H.normalizer.subtype_injective.injOn
    rw [← Subgroup.coe_map, MonoidHom.map_closure, Set.image_pair]
    exact Set.finite_coe_iff.mp (hG (a : G) ((g : G)⁻¹ * a * g))
  -- Its image in `N_G(H)/H` is `⟨ā, ā^ḡ⟩`, which is therefore finite as well.
  have h₂ : (Subgroup.closure {a, g⁻¹ * a * g}).map
      (QuotientGroup.mk' (H.subgroupOf H.normalizer)) = Subgroup.closure
        {QuotientGroup.mk a,
          (QuotientGroup.mk g)⁻¹ * QuotientGroup.mk a * QuotientGroup.mk g} := by
    rw [MonoidHom.map_closure, Set.image_pair]
    rfl
  rw [← h₂]
  exact Set.finite_coe_iff.mpr (by rw [Subgroup.coe_map]; exact h₁.image _)

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_isBinaryFinite_multiplicative_int : ¬ IsBinaryFinite (Multiplicative ℤ) := by
  intro h
  have hfin := h (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1) (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1)
  rw [Set.pair_eq_singleton, ← Subgroup.zpowers_eq_closure] at hfin
  have : (Subgroup.zpowers (Multiplicative.ofAdd (1 : ℤ)) : Set (Multiplicative ℤ)).Infinite :=
    infinite_zpowers.mpr <| by
      rw [isOfFinOrder_ofAdd_iff, isOfFinAddOrder_iff_nsmul_eq_zero]
      simp
  exact this (Set.toFinite _)

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no existence question (answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ G, ...) whose conjuncts must all be hypotheses joined by ∧, not implications: G periodic (torsion), residually finite, an F*-group in Shunkov's sense as defined in Archive problem 7.42 (roughly: for every finite subgroup H and every element a of prime order in N_G(H)/H, the subgroups ⟨a, a^g⟩ with g ∈ N_G(H)/H are finite — the Archive text is not in the sandbox, so the formalizer must take the exact definition from there), every Sylow p-subgroup (maximal p-subgroup) finite for every prime p, and G not binary finite (i.e. some two elements generate an infinite subgroup); the added hypothesis 'residually finite' is what distinguishes this from the earlier 7.42 version, so it must not be dropped.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state mathematically the same thing: answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), torsion ∧ residually finite ∧ F*-group ∧ (∀ prime p, ∀ P : Sylow p G, Finite P) ∧ ¬ binary finite, with every condition a conjunct (no implications) and the distinguishing 'residually finite' hypothesis retained. Mathlib's `Sylow p G` is the type of maximal p-subgroups of an arbitrary group, which is the correct notion of Sylow subgroup for infinite groups; p is restricted to primes so the degenerate `Sylow 0 G` is excluded. `Monoid.IsTorsion` is exactly 'every element has finite order'. The bespoke F*-definition follows Shunkov's 'conjugately biprimitively finite' condition as recorded in Archive 7.42 (for every finite subgroup H, including the trivial one, every prime-order a in N_G(H)/H and every g in N_G(H)/H, ⟨a, a^g⟩ is finite); prime order is `(orderOf a).Prime`, which correctly excludes infinite-order elements (orderOf = 0). Boundary check: the trivial group satisfies all positive conjuncts but fails ¬ binary finite, so the existential is not trivially witnessed; ℤ is not binary finite (proved as a test) so the negated conjunct is non-vacuous. c06 chosen as base for its clean variable-style definitions and the nontrivial proved sanity lemma (binary finite ⇒ F*-group); I added c07's proved test that ℤ is not binary finite and expanded the docstrings. c05 (Set.Finite / homomorphism-based residual finiteness) and c02/c03 (`let Q` in a def, `[Finite H]` instance binder) are equivalent but stylistically weaker; c07's `[Fact p.Prime]` binder is equivalent to `p.Prime →` but less readable.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.78

by V. P. Shunkov

Does there exist a periodic residually finite $F^{*}$-group (see Archive, 7.42) all of
whose Sylow subgroups are finite and which is not binary finite?

Here a group $G$ is an $F^{*}$-group in the sense of V. P. Shunkov (Kourovka Notebook,
Archive, 7.42) if for every finite subgroup $H$ of $G$ and every element $a$ of prime order
in $N_G(H)/H$, all the subgroups $\langle a, a^g \rangle$, $g \in N_G(H)/H$, are finite.
A Sylow $p$-subgroup of an arbitrary group is a maximal $p$-subgroup. A group is
*binary finite* if any two of its elements generate a finite subgroup.

The requirement that the group be residually finite is what distinguishes this problem
from Archive problem 7.42.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.78»

variable (G : Type*) [Group G]

/-- A group $G$ is *residually finite* if every non-identity element lies outside some
normal subgroup of finite index, i.e. the intersection of all normal subgroups of finite
index of $G$ is trivial. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

/-- A group is *binary finite* if any two of its elements generate a finite subgroup. -/
def IsBinaryFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- A group $G$ is an *$F^{*}$-group* (V. P. Shunkov, Kourovka Notebook, Archive, 7.42) if
for every finite subgroup $H$ of $G$ and every element $a$ of prime order in the quotient
$N_G(H)/H$, the subgroups $\langle a, a^g \rangle$, $g \in N_G(H)/H$, are all finite.
Here $a^g = g^{-1} a g$. -/
def IsFStarGroup : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H →
    ∀ a g : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      (orderOf a).Prime → Finite (Subgroup.closure {a, g⁻¹ * a * g})

variable {G}

/-- A finite group is residually finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsResiduallyFinite.of_finite [Finite G] : IsResiduallyFinite G :=
  fun _ hg => ⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance, by simpa using hg⟩

/-- A finite group is binary finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBinaryFinite.of_finite [Finite G] : IsBinaryFinite G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A finite group is an $F^{*}$-group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFStarGroup.of_finite [Finite G] : IsFStarGroup G :=
  fun _ _ _ _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A binary finite group is an $F^{*}$-group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBinaryFinite.isFStarGroup (hG : IsBinaryFinite G) : IsFStarGroup G := by
  intro H _ a g _
  induction a using QuotientGroup.induction_on with | H a
  induction g using QuotientGroup.induction_on with | H g
  -- `⟨a, a^g⟩` is finite in `N_G(H)`: it embeds into the finite subgroup `⟨a, a^g⟩` of `G`.
  have h₁ : (Subgroup.closure {a, g⁻¹ * a * g} : Set H.normalizer).Finite := by
    refine Set.Finite.of_finite_image (f := H.normalizer.subtype) ?_
      H.normalizer.subtype_injective.injOn
    rw [← Subgroup.coe_map, MonoidHom.map_closure, Set.image_pair]
    exact Set.finite_coe_iff.mp (hG (a : G) ((g : G)⁻¹ * a * g))
  -- Its image in `N_G(H)/H` is `⟨ā, ā^ḡ⟩`, which is therefore finite as well.
  have h₂ : (Subgroup.closure {a, g⁻¹ * a * g}).map
      (QuotientGroup.mk' (H.subgroupOf H.normalizer)) = Subgroup.closure
        {QuotientGroup.mk a,
          (QuotientGroup.mk g)⁻¹ * QuotientGroup.mk a * QuotientGroup.mk g} := by
    rw [MonoidHom.map_closure, Set.image_pair]
    rfl
  rw [← h₂]
  exact Set.finite_coe_iff.mpr (by rw [Subgroup.coe_map]; exact h₁.image _)

/-- The infinite cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}$ is not binary finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_isBinaryFinite_multiplicative_int : ¬ IsBinaryFinite (Multiplicative ℤ) := by
  intro h
  have hfin := h (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1) (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1)
  rw [Set.pair_eq_singleton, ← Subgroup.zpowers_eq_closure] at hfin
  have : (Subgroup.zpowers (Multiplicative.ofAdd (1 : ℤ)) : Set (Multiplicative ℤ)).Infinite :=
    infinite_zpowers.mpr <| by
      rw [isOfFinOrder_ofAdd_iff, isOfFinAddOrder_iff_nsmul_eq_zero]
      simp
  exact this (Set.toFinite _)

/--
Does there exist a periodic residually finite $F^{*}$-group (see Archive, 7.42) all of
whose Sylow subgroups are finite and which is not binary finite?

Here "periodic" means that every element has finite order; $G$ is an $F^{*}$-group if for
every finite subgroup $H$ of $G$ and every element $a$ of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$, the
subgroups $\langle a, a^g \rangle$, $g \in N_G(H)/H$, are finite; "all Sylow subgroups are
finite" means that for every prime $p$ every maximal $p$-subgroup of $G$ is finite; and
$G$ is binary finite if any two of its elements generate a finite subgroup.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.78» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      Monoid.IsTorsion G ∧ IsResiduallyFinite G ∧ IsFStarGroup G ∧
      (∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, Finite P) ∧ ¬ IsBinaryFinite G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.78»

items: F*-group definition: the Archive text of 7.42 was not available in the sandbox (no internet). I used the definition given in the decomposition notes, which coincides with my own recollection of the Archive entry: G is an F*-group if for every finite subgroup H and every element a of prime order in N_G(H)/H, all subgroups ⟨a, a^g⟩ (g ∈ N_G(H)/H) are finite (i.e. N_G(H)/H is 'conjugately biprimitively finite' for every finite H). A reviewer with access to the Archive should verify this wording — this is the main residual risk.
a^g is formalized as g⁻¹ * a * g (standard right-conjugation convention); since g ranges over the whole quotient, the direction is immaterial.

'Sylow subgroup' is taken in the sense used for arbitrary (infinite) groups: a maximal p-subgroup, which is exactly Mathlib's `Sylow p G`. Quantified over all primes p (`p.Prime →`), so `Sylow p G` is never used with a non-prime p.
'Periodic' is formalized as `Monoid.IsTorsion G` (every element has finite order).
Residually finite is formalized via finite-index normal subgroups rather than homomorphisms to finite groups; the two are equivalent.
The group is quantified as `G : Type` (universe 0), following the other Kourovka files (1_74, 19_25).

Four `@[category test]` lemmas with full proofs were added as basic API tests for the bespoke definitions (finite groups satisfy all three; binary finite ⇒ F*-group). The generic definitions (residually finite, binary finite) are kept in the problem file because the task restricts output to a single file; a maintainer may prefer to move them to FormalConjecturesForMathlib.
Boundary check: the trivial group satisfies all positive conjuncts but is binary finite, so the existential is not trivially satisfied.

reviewer_notes: The Archive 7.42 text is not in the sandbox; the F*-group definition used (for every finite subgroup H and every element a of prime order in N_G(H)/H, all ⟨a, a^g⟩ with g ∈ N_G(H)/H are finite) matches the decomposition notes and Shunkov's standard notion of conjugately biprimitively finite groups. A reviewer with the Archive should confirm the wording; this is the main residual risk, and it is a risk shared by all candidates (none omitted or objected). Conjugation convention a^g = g⁻¹ a g is immaterial since g ranges over the whole quotient. The three generic definitions (IsResiduallyFinite, IsBinaryFinite, IsFStarGroup) are kept in the problem file; a maintainer may prefer moving IsResiduallyFinite / IsBinaryFinite to FormalConjecturesForMathlib. Final file compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning.
